display.purpose: The contact sign-off wordmark at 9.5rem (7.6rem mobile). Appears exactly once on the entire site — the one loud moment that lets everything else stay quiet.

headline.purpose: Base h1 at 2.85rem / weight 500. Standalone section titles. Note the hero deliberately overrides this down to 1.9rem so the bordered intro panel keeps its composure.

title.purpose: h3 and the experience company name at 1.7rem / weight 400. Weight drops to 400 here; below this level hierarchy is size alone.

subtitle.purpose: h4 at 1.425rem / weight 400. Also the size of social and CV action icons.

body.purpose: All prose and nav links at 0.95rem / line-height 1.6. This is the base unit — every other size in the codebase is a multiple of it.

label.purpose: Experience field labels, dates, locations at 0.855rem (0.9x base), recessed to 70-80% opacity. Never recessed by weight.

emphasis.purpose: The .highlight class at weight 700. Keyword emphasis in prose is carried by weight only — never colour, never the gradient treatment. Works identically in both performance modes.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: The universal state transition. Every hover, opacity change, and border brighten in the system uses this exact value. There is no second duration for state.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Section and card entrances: translateY(8px) into place, exposed as --reveal-distance / --reveal-duration / --reveal-stagger (40ms step when several land together). Pure CSS keyframes fired once by a single shared IntersectionObserver in lib/reveal.ts.

motion.name: nav-entrance
motion.purpose: The navbar slides down from translateY(-100%) on page load. Neutralised by the prefers-reduced-motion block.

motion.name: navbar-glass
motion.purpose: Backdrop-filter and background-color crossfade as the navbar transitions from transparent to blurred on first scroll.

motion.name: marquee-forward
motion.purpose: Top tech-stack row. Deliberately coprime-ish with the reverse row so the two never resync.

motion.name: gradient-flow
motion.purpose: Shimmer on the hero name, implemented with background-clip: text, which the system bans — slated for replacement with solid Signal White. Disabled in low-perf mode.

motion.name: timeline-pulse
motion.purpose: Two offset rings expanding scale(1) to scale(3.2) from the active experience dot, second ring delayed 1.2s. Disabled in low-perf mode.

motion.name: description-reveal
motion.purpose: Project card description fades opacity 0 to 1 on hover or focus-within. It holds its space at all times, so the row height never reflows.

components.name: Panel
components.description: The base container of the system: a transparent hairline rectangle that brightens its border on hover. Never filled — the shader shows through.

Solutions Engineer Intern

components.css: .ds-project-card { position: relative; display: block; background: #000; color: var(--primary-color, #fff); font-family: var(--font-family, Manrope, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5); border-radius: 5px; cursor: pointer; transition: border 0.3s ease-out; } .ds-project-card:hover, .ds-project-card:focus-within { border-color: rgba(255,255,255,1); } .ds-status { position: absolute; top: 1rem; left: 1rem; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.855rem; opacity: 0.7; } .ds-status-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 100%; } .ds-status-dot--live { background: green; } .ds-project-inner { padding: 2rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; text-align: center; } .ds-project-title { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.25; margin: 0; } .ds-project-desc { font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1.6; margin: 0.4rem 0 0; max-height: 0; overflow: hidden; opacity: 0; transition: max-height 1s ease-in-out, opacity 0.3s ease-out; } .ds-project-card:hover .ds-project-desc, .ds-project-card:focus-within .ds-project-desc { max-height: 300px; opacity: 1; } .ds-project-links { display: flex; gap: 1rem; margin-top: 0.5rem; } .ds-project-link { color: var(--primary-color, #fff); opacity: 0.5; display: flex; border-radius: 5px; transition: opacity 0.3s ease-out; } .ds-project-link:hover { opacity: 1; } .ds-project-link:focus-visible { opacity: 1; outline: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,1); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Vertical Rail
components.description: Signature component. A narrow full-height hairline rail with vertical-rl label and a bottom chevron, used as a call-to-action edge beside the hero and the projects grid. Nothing in a template ships this.

components.name: Social Card

components.css: .ds-social { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; height: 50px; padding: 0.4rem; background: #000; color: var(--primary-color, #fff); font-family: var(--font-family, Manrope, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif); font-size: 0.95rem; text-decoration: none; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5); border-radius: 5px; transition: border 0.3s ease-out, scale 0.3s ease-out; } .ds-social:hover { border-color: rgba(255,255,255,1); scale: 1.1; } .ds-social:focus-visible { border-color: rgba(255,255,255,1); outline: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,1); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-social-tile { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1/1; border-radius: 5px; color: #fff; } .ds-social-tile--linkedin { background: #007BFF; } .ds-social-tile--github { background: #595959; } .ds-social-tile--instagram { background: #DD2A7B; } .ds-social-tile--email { background: #B9B9B9; } .ds-social-label { padding-right: 0.4rem; } @media (max-width: 1180px) { .ds-social:hover { scale: 1; } }

components.name: Timeline Dot
components.description: A 14px hairline circle filled with the substrate so it interrupts the timeline spine rather than crossing it. The active variant fills green and emits two offset pulse rings.
components.css: .ds-timeline { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2.5rem; padding: 1rem 2rem; background: #000; } .ds-timeline::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 1rem; bottom: 1rem; left: calc(2rem + 6px); width: 1px; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(255,255,255,0.35) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.35) calc(100% - 1.5rem), rgba(255,255,255,0) 100%); } .ds-timeline-dot { position: relative; z-index: 1; width: 14px; height: 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.8); border-radius: 100%; background: #000; } .ds-timeline-dot--active { background: green; border-color: green; } .ds-timeline-dot--active::before, .ds-timeline-dot--active::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -1px; border: 1px solid green; border-radius: 100%; opacity: 0; animation: ds-pulse 2.4s ease-out infinite; } .ds-timeline-dot--active::after { animation-delay: 1.2s; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0% { opacity: 0.55; transform: scale(1); } 70%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(3.2); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-timeline-dot--active::before, .ds-timeline-dot--active::after { animation: none; } }

components.name: Perf Mode Toggle
components.description: Signature component. A 22px bolt in the navbar that swaps the whole site between data-perf high and low — unmounting the WebGL shader, tearing down the smooth-scroll RAF loop, and stripping every always-on animation. Persisted to localStorage and applied pre-paint so there is no flash.

Click to turn the animated background off."><svg width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="M12 2a10 10 0 1 0 0 20 10 10 0 0 0 0-20zm1 4-5 7h3.2l-1.2 5 5-7h-3.2z"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-perf-toggle { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 22px; height: 22px; padding: 0; margin: 0; background: none; border: none; border-radius: 5px; color: var(--primary-color, #fff); opacity: 0.5; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.3s ease-out; } .ds-perf-toggle:hover { opacity: 1; } .ds-perf-toggle:focus-visible { opacity: 1; outline: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,1); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-perf-toggle[aria-pressed='false'] { opacity: 0.5; }

components.css: .ds-back-to-top { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 3rem; height: 3rem; background: #000; color: var(--primary-color, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--primary-color, #fff); border-radius: 100%; opacity: 0.5; cursor: pointer; transform: translateY(0); transition: opacity 0.3s ease-out, transform 0.3s ease-out; } .ds-back-to-top:hover { opacity: 1; } .ds-back-to-top:focus-visible { opacity: 1; outline: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,1); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-back-to-top[hidden], .ds-back-to-top.is-hidden { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(100px); pointer-events: none; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-back-to-top { transition: opacity 0.3s ease-out; } }

narrative.overview:
This is a black cabin at night with one light source. Every surface is a hairline-ruled panel floating on a void, and the only colour in the entire system is a slow electric-blue reactor glowing behind everything at a distance. Nothing is filled, nothing is shadowed, nothing is decorated. The system reads the way a well-designed cockpit reads: dense with information, absolutely legible, and completely uninterested in impressing you on first glance.

The interaction model follows from the metaphor. Instruments sit at rest in half-light — every link, card, icon, and social tile defaults to 50% opacity — and come up to full brightness the moment you touch them. That single gesture, opacity 0.5 to 1 over 0.3s ease-out, is essentially the entire interaction vocabulary of the site. There are no fills, no colour shifts, no scale bounces. Attention is a light coming on.

This system explicitly rejects the four things PRODUCT.md names. It is not a generic template portfolio — there is no theme vocabulary here, no purchased section grammar, and the structural units (the vertical rotated-text call-to-action rail, the dual counter-scrolling tech marquees, the perf-mode reactor kill switch) do not exist in any starter kit. It is not SaaS landing-page grammar — there are no hero metric blocks, no gradient blobs, no tracked uppercase eyebrows, no 01 / 02 / 03 markers. It is not a scroll-jacked showreel — Lenis smooths the scroll but never hijacks it, and reveals fire once and stay put. It is not a dev-resume wall — skills appear as a moving marquee at half-light, never as a badge grid or a proficiency bar.
keyCharacteristics: Pure #000000 substrate. Not near-black, not charcoal, not a tinted neutral.
Exactly one border weight: 1px, via --border-px. Every rule in the system is a hairline.
Exactly one corner radius: 5px. Circles (100%) only for dots and the back-to-top.
One typeface, Manrope variable, carrying the whole hierarchy on weight and size alone.
A single base unit of 0.95rem from which every type size in the codebase is derived.
Zero shadows. Depth is opacity and blur, never elevation.
Colour lives behind the content plane, never on it.
A user-facing performance switch that degrades the whole system gracefully.

rules.name: The Blue Stays Behind Glass Rule
rules.body: Reactor Blue exists only on the shader plane and in ::selection. It must never appear as a button background, a heading colour, a border, a link state, or a gradient on the content plane. The entire tension of the design is a monochrome instrument floating over a coloured light it never touches. The moment blue crosses onto a surface, the metaphor collapses and the page becomes an ordinary dark-mode site with an accent colour.

rules.name: The Two-State Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element has exactly two visual states: resting at 50% opacity, and active at 100%. Not three, not a colour shift, not a background fill. If a component needs a third state, it needs a rethink, not a new token.

rules.name: The Black Is Black Rule
rules.body: The substrate is #000000 and nothing else. No #0a0a0a, no #111, no warm-tinted near-black, no 'softer on the eyes' charcoal. The shader needs true black to read as a light source rather than a panel.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Colour Rule
rules.body: Emphasis in prose is font-weight: 700 and nothing else. No accent-coloured keywords, no underlines, no highlight backgrounds. The .highlight class is the entire mechanism.

rules.name: The One Loud Moment Rule
rules.body: 9.5rem display type appears exactly once on the site, in the contact sign-off. If a second element wants that scale, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Zero box-shadow declarations. If an element needs to separate from its surroundings, raise its border opacity or give it more space. Never add a shadow, a glow, or a lighter background panel.

rules.name: The Two Glass Surfaces Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter appears on the scrolled navbar and the CV caption. That is the complete list. Every additional blurred surface pushes the system toward the glassmorphism it bans, and costs a GPU layer that low-perf mode then has to unwind.

rules.name: The Transparent Container Rule
rules.body: Containers are outlined, never filled. background-color on a card or panel is a bug — it occludes the shader and breaks the floating-instrument metaphor.

rules.name: The One Easing Rule
rules.body: Every state transition is 0.3s ease-out (--state-duration). Entrance reveals are 0.4s ease-out over 8px (--reveal-duration / --reveal-distance), stepped by 40ms (--reveal-stagger) when several land together. There is no third duration and no other easing curve in the system.

dos: Do keep the substrate at exactly #000000 and let the shader be the only light source.
Do derive every new font-size as a multiple of the 0.95rem base unit. Pick a multiplier from the table in the Typography section, not a pixel value.
Do use 1px (var(--border-px)) for every rule, border, and divider. One weight, no exceptions.
Do use 5px for every rectangle and 100% for every dot.
Do express state with the two-state opacity gesture: 0.5 at rest, 1 on contact, 0.3s ease-out.
Do use the decomposed --primary-r/g/b channels when a component needs a custom alpha, rather than adding a new colour token.
Do pair every new always-on animation with a html[data-perf="low"] override in the same change.

Do add a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block alongside it — the perf toggle is a preference, the media query is an accessibility requirement, and PRODUCT.md targets WCAG 2.1 AA. Both now exist and live together in styles/motion.css, so neither can be added without the other being obvious.

Do rely on the single global :focus-visible treatment in styles/base.css (1px outline, 4px offset, full opacity) and never reset outline in a component. A blanket outline: none leaves a control focusable with nothing to show for it, which is why none remain in src/.

Do ship interactive elements as real <a> and <button> elements. The logo, the back-to-top control, the three vertical rails, the bio and role toggles, and the technology category controls are all native elements — there is no div with a click handler left in the codebase.

Do verify half-light text against the brightest frame of the moving shader, not against flat black. #FFFFFF at 50% over the reactor's bright pole is materially worse than the same white over #000000, and the shader is the real backdrop.
Do give the project status dots a non-colour companion (label or shape). Colour-only encoding fails AA.
donts: Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Gradient text is an absolute ban. The .gradient-animation treatment currently on the name in the hero is exactly this pattern and should be replaced with solid Signal White plus weight; the low-perf branch already renders it that way and reads better.
Don't let Reactor Blue onto the content plane. No blue buttons, no blue headings, no blue borders, no blue gradients. It lives behind the glass.
Don't add a box-shadow anywhere. Zero exist; keep it that way.
Don't add a third blurred surface. The scrolled navbar and the CV caption are the complete list.
Don't fill a card or panel with a background colour. Containers are outlines.
Don't use border-left or border-right above 1px as a coloured accent stripe. The experience role indent is a 1px structural rule and is the only left-border permitted.
Don't add a second typeface. Manrope carries the whole hierarchy on weight and size deliberately; a display serif or a mono would be costume.

Don't ship the generic template portfolio look — Framer / Notion / Astro-theme section grammar, stock hero layouts, or any component that looks like it came with a starter kit. This is PRODUCT.md's primary anti-reference and the site's entire premise is that it was built, not bought.

Don't import SaaS landing-page grammar: hero metric blocks, gradient blobs, three identical rounded-icon feature cards, tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above section headings, or 01 / 02 / 03 numbered section markers.

Don't build a scroll-jacked showreel. Lenis smooths the scroll; it must never seize it. Reveals fire once and stay put, and no reveal may gate content visibility — if the transition never fires, the section must still be there.
Don't build a dev-resume wall: badge grids, skill percentage bars, or exhaustive technology lists. Skills belong in the half-light marquee, and claims belong behind a link to something running.
Don't signal an active navigation item or a project status with colour or opacity alone.
Don't introduce a warm or tinted neutral anywhere. This system is #000000 and #FFFFFF at varying alpha, and that austerity is the point.
